purpose: Validate the existing island-pollination mechanism stack against multiple admitted propagation states without making Campanula microdonta, Issue #91, or any single focal taxon a programme-wide blocker.

synthetic_buffering_state.interpretation: local support/network context can rescue effective-service and reproductive sign in two frozen stochastic blocks but can also worsen matched declines

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: physical access failure -> directional pollen transfer -> morph-specific fruit asymmetry
signed functional mismatch -> contact/robbing/resource change -> high reproductive performance
qualitative_validation_targets.role: buffering boundary case whose qualitative state is now synthetically available but whose empirical buffer mechanism remains unmapped

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: common-ish matching decline -> divergent pollen and floral responses
qualitative_validation_targets.role: branching case; Campanula is not the only lineage
qualitative_validation_targets.do_not_require: direct Issue #91 field dependency to retain the observed multi-taxon branching pattern

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: frozen signed-position prediction -> observed selection direction opposite or nonconcordant
island selfing/corolla difference without detected current island service deficit
qualitative_validation_targets.role: establishment_or_assurance alternative case; a synthetic buffering class exists but the historical/establishment mapping is unresolved

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: large visitor-assemblage/visitation contrast -> similar self/outcross seed-set index and negligible autogamy, but Mona open reproduction is pollen limited relative to outcross and realized multiplicative fitness is lower
qualitative_validation_targets.role: axis-decoupling constraint, not a whole-reproduction buffering case

validation_question: Can one frozen mechanism architecture generate or accommodate the observed diversity of propagation states across independent island systems without parameter tuning to any one focal taxon, while keeping distinct reproductive axes separate?
success_is: the mechanism can generate branching and a buffering state under predeclared structural differences
empirical systems are not assigned a synthetic buffer mechanism without source-native mapping
axis-decoupling constraints are retained rather than forced into propagate/buffer bins
no single system-specific parameter rescue is required
next_gate: Freeze empirical network-context predictions and require source-native visitor-specific rate x effectiveness or another matched support/service mapping before assigning the replicated synthetic network-buffering route to a real island system.
claim_boundary: This registry defines qualitative validation targets only. It is not a pooled effect-size model, does not convert heterogeneous estimands into one coefficient, and does not claim that a synthetic buffering class empirically identifies the mechanism behind Hawaiʻi, Nicotiana, Guaiacum, or any other system.
